title: Model alias flattening and client mapper library for legacy alias routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Over time we have accumulated multiple model aliases (eg. 'gptx-std', 'gptx-beta', 'gptx-v1-compat') that resolve to overlapping model binaries. This alias proliferation creates complexity for routing, telemetry, billing, and rollout consistency. Goal: Flatten aliases to a canonical model identifier per model family and provide a first-party client-side 'alias-mapper' library and migration contract to customers so client code can transparently translate legacy aliases to the canonical id during a phased sunset. This reduces runtime routing indirection, simplifies kernel selection, and reduces cross-compat confusion while limiting customer disruption.
context_and_background: We currently support alias-level rollouts and fallbacks; however, alias drift has led to divergent behavior where the same alias routes differently across regions and releases. Enterprise customers with hardcoded aliases in SDKs and server-side adapters have the highest friction during decommissioning. Previous deprecation initiatives focused on transport/protocol changes; this ticket is focused on model routing alias normalization and enabling low-effort client-side migration.
objectives: Define canonical id naming and authoritative mapping for all active aliases in the 'gptx' and 'rwd-infer' families
Ship a client mapper library (TS/Go/Python) that exposes a single call to translate legacy alias -> canonical id
Provide per-customer migration contracts (30/60/90 day windows) with optional reverse-lookup support to minimize application churn
Ensure runtime and routing systems accept both alias and canonical id for a graceful transition and then enforce canonical-only after end-of-life window
out_of_scope: Automated rewrites inside third-party SDKs (we will provide guidance and a library only)
Changing model binaries or retraining models as part of this effort
Large-scale customer migrations requiring on-prem software installs (handled case-by-case via engagement)
proposed_solution_summary: Identify authoritative mapping in a source-of-truth table maintained by model onboarding. Implement a 'compat' layer in the control plane that consults the mapping for requests in the transition window. Publish a lightweight open-source 'alias-mapper' package in TypeScript, Python, and Go that caches the mapping and exposes an async refresh. Offer an opt-in server-side middleware snippet for customers who prefer a drop-in adapter. Coordinate a phased sunset per-customer with clear telemetry gates and rollback criteria.
migration_steps: Inventory: generate canonical mapping export for 'gptx' and 'rwd-infer' families (ENG audit task)
Build: implement alias-mapper libraries (TS/Python/Go) with caching and ETag-based refresh
Control plane: add transition flag that allows both alias and canonical id for 90 days
SDKs: release minor versions that call alias-mapper by default with opt-out flag
Customer outreach: publish migration contract template and per-customer mapping report
Per-customer run: enable 30/60/90 day windows, monitor telemetry and escalate for bespoke needs
Enforce: after 90-day EOL, reject alias-based requests with 410 and guidance header
acceptance_criteria: Authoritative mapping published and accessible via internal API and public artifact
Alias-mapper library released in TS/Python/Go with CI, unit tests, and example integrations
Control plane transition flag implemented and tested in staging; runtime accepts both ids during window
SDKs updated to include alias-mapper and default to mapping on startup with opt-out config
At least three pilot enterprise customers complete the 30-day mapping window without service-impact incidents
Telemetry gates set: <0.1% 5xx increase, token-latency P95 delta < 10ms during pilot
Deprecation docs and per-customer migration contract template published in Console Docs
telemetry_gates: Baseline P95 token latency by model family recorded prior to pilot
During pilot: 5xx rate change must be <= 0.1% absolute increase
Client-mapper error rate < 0.01% in production traffic for pilot customers
Mapping cache hit ratio >= 99% in steady state
rollback_criteria: If customer-facing 5xx rate increases > 0.5% absolute for any pilot customer, pause that customer's enforced timeline
If model selection divergence causes > 1% correctness regressions on tracked eval sets, revert control-plane mapping enforcement
If alias-mapper library rollback metrics show memory leaks or repeated refresh failures, pull SDK releases and patch
operational_requirements: Control-plane feature flagging for per-tenant enforcement; migrations dashboard that surfaces alias usage (top aliases per customer), SDK adoption, and EOL readiness. Support runbooks for account teams to open tickets and request bespoke windows. Ensure billing and metering pipelines understand canonical id mapping for backfill reconciliation.
customer_communication: Publish a 'Model Alias Flattening' migration guide that includes: per-customer mapping report, suggested integration snippets, opt-out instructions, and timelines. Send targeted emails to customers with active usage of deprecated aliases and schedule account review calls. Provide a GA date, final enforcement date, and an emergency rollback plan.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Customers hardcode aliases in many services. Mitigation: provide library and server-side middleware and offer 90/180-day contractual windows for high-risk customers.
Risk: Telemetry and billing reconciliation disagreements after alias collapse. Mitigation: run reconciliation job and provide transparent mapping SKU reports for the billing team.
Risk: SDK adoption lag. Mitigation: ship backward-compatible SDKs that include opt-in mapping earlier and provide an 'adapter' middleware for quick adoption.
notes: Coordinate with Legal for per-customer contract addendum when offering extended windows. Track progress in the Endpoint Consolidation board. Include I/O and kernel selection teams in the alpha rollout.
